name: The Stillglass Pond
region_detail: Within the deeper northeastern woods, in a sheltered depression surrounded by mature trees.
site_type: pond | Natural wonders; supernatural sites | Unnaturally tranquil woodland pool.
history: Hollowbough oral tradition preserves accounts of a perfectly circular pond whose waters reflect the forest as it appeared in earlier ages. The pool has long been avoided by some travelers, although others visit it for quiet contemplation or to observe traces of the woodland’s former inhabitants.
current_state: The pond remains still even in strong winds. Its reflections generally resemble the surrounding woodland, but occasionally reveal unfamiliar buildings, pathways, or trees absent from the present shore. Fallen leaves accumulate around its margin without noticeably disturbing the central surface.
inhabitants: Woodland wildlife and occasional Hollowbough visitors. No permanent or supernatural inhabitants are established.
danger_level: Low along the shore; uncertain if the water is entered.
points_of_interest:
Circular pool; ring of mature trees; still reflective surface; narrow shore; old path ending at the water; a flat stone suitable for observation.

Unresolved elements: Whether the reflections depict actual history, alternative possibilities, or another place entirely; What determines when the reflected landscape changes; Whether entering the water has any supernatural consequences; Whether the reflected paths or structures can be located in the present forest.
discovery: Within the deeper northeastern woods, in a sheltered depression surrounded by mature trees. Saelis Moonthorn knows an old tale describing the trees surrounding the pond. Hollowbough guides may identify the depression from that description.
related_records:
Rumor: R-TH-017 — The Mirror Pond — Direct. The pool and its reflections of earlier landscapes are the subject of the rumor.

Notable individuals and factions: Saelis Moonthorn (N-040) — familiar with the tale and its warning against entering the water; Hollowbough travelers — may know customary approaches or accounts of earlier observations.
